html:
The Zacatecos were a Native American people of the high, dry plateau of what is now Zacatecas and Durango in northern Mexico. They were one of the nomadic peoples the Aztecs and Spanish lumped together as Chichimecs.

They lived by hunting and gathering, especially mesquite and prickly pear. In 1546 Spaniards found rich silver at Zacatecas, in their land. Mines, towns and wagon roads to Mexico City followed, and the Zacatecos and their neighbours the Guachichiles attacked them. This began the long Chichimeca War, from about 1550 to 1590.

New Spain ended the war mostly by paying for peace with food and cloth, and by settling farmers from central Mexico among the nomads. By the 1700s the Zacatecos had been absorbed or had died out. See also Zacateco on the modern map.
